title: Artificial Intelligence: Council gives final green light to simplify and streamline rules
date_evidence: Council of the EU  Press release  29 June 2026 14:30  Artificial Intelligence: Council gives final green light to simplify and streamline rules
key_claim: On 29 June 2026 the Council gave final adoption to the Digital Omnibus on AI, deferring high-risk AI obligations to 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (embedded systems) and adding a prohibition on AI-generated CSAM and non-consensual intimate imagery.
frame_summary: The EU has formally adopted a simplification of the AI Act that defers its high-risk obligations to keep Europe competitive.
verbatim_quote: Given that provisions on high-risk AI systems were due to enter into force on 2 August 2026, the co-legislators treated this part of the package with utmost priority and agreed on a fixed timeline for the delayed application of high-risk rules: the new application dates would be 2 December 2027 for stand-alone high-risk AI systems and 2 August 2028 for high-risk AI systems embedded in products.

title: EU agrees Digital Omnibus deal to simplify AI rules
date_evidence: EU agrees Digital Omnibus deal to simplify AI rules  Alert  14 May 2026
key_claim: The Digital Omnibus on AI, provisionally agreed 7 May 2026, is a package of targeted AI Act amendments delaying high-risk deadlines to 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 and adding a CSAM/nudifier prohibition.
frame_summary: The Digital Omnibus on AI is a package of targeted AI Act amendments that delays high-risk enforcement deadlines to give business more time.
verbatim_quote: The provisional agreement introduces a fixed timeline for the delayed application of the bulk of the rules governing high-risk AI systems

title: Omnibus Simplification of EU's Sustainability Rules (CSRD and CSDDD) Enacted
key_claim: The EU Amendment Directive (EU) 2026/470 simplifying CSRD and CSDDD was published 26 February 2026 and entered into force 18 March 2026; CSRD transposition is due 19 March 2027 and CSDDD compliance only from July 2029.
frame_summary: The EU has enacted an Omnibus directive that sharply narrows CSRD and CSDDD sustainability obligations and pushes back deadlines.
verbatim_quote: On February 26, 2026, the Amendment Directive (EU) 2026/470 significantly simplifying corporate sustainability reporting (CSRD) and corporate sustainability due diligence (CSDDD) requirements has been officially published and shall enter into force twenty days following publication on March 18, 2026.

title: Digital Omnibus: EDPB and EDPS support simplification and competitiveness while raising key concerns
date_evidence: Digital Omnibus: EDPB and EDPS support simplification and competitiveness while raising key concerns  11 February 2026  Brussels, 11 February - the EDPB and the EDPS have adopted a Joint Opinion on the Digital Omnibus Regulation proposal.
key_claim: In Joint Opinion 2/2026 the EDPB and EDPS back the Digital Omnibus simplification aims but strongly urge co-legislators not to adopt the proposed narrowing of the definition of personal data in the GDPR.
frame_summary: EU data-protection regulators back simplification but warn that redefining personal data would gut the GDPR's scope.
verbatim_quote: The EDPB and the EDPS strongly urge the co-legislators not to adopt the proposed changes to the definition of personal data

title: Treasury Proposes Rule to Implement the GENIUS Act's Requirements to Counter Illicit Finance
date_evidence: Press Releases  Treasury Proposes Rule to Implement the GENIUS Act's Requirements to Counter Illicit Finance  April 8, 2026
key_claim: On 8 April 2026 Treasury's FinCEN and OFAC issued a joint proposed rule treating permitted payment stablecoin issuers as Bank Secrecy Act financial institutions with anti-money-laundering and sanctions duties.
frame_summary: The US Treasury is building the federal stablecoin regime by imposing bank-style anti-money-laundering and sanctions duties on issuers.
signals_supported: US GENIUS Act stablecoin rulemaking build-out
cluster: Multilateral rulebooks splinter into national tracks
verbatim_quote: Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a joint proposed rule to implement provisions of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act).

title: GENIUS Act deadline puts stablecoin issuers on the clock
key_claim: The GENIUS Act's one-year statutory rulemaking deadline of 18 July 2026 requires federal regulators, Treasury and state regulators to finalise stablecoin-issuer access rules; the Act then takes effect 120 days after finalisation.
frame_summary: A statutory 18 July deadline is forcing US regulators to convert the GENIUS Act into concrete stablecoin-issuer access rules.
signals_supported: US GENIUS Act stablecoin rulemaking build-out
cluster: Multilateral rulebooks splinter into national tracks
verbatim_quote: Regulators have until July 18, 2026, to turn the GENIUS Act from a statute into access rules for stablecoin issuers that want a clear regulatory path into the US.

title: Newest version of crypto Clarity Act may drop as soon as next week, sources say
key_claim: The US Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, merging Senate Banking and Agriculture texts, could reach the Senate floor the week of 20 July 2026 but still lacks the Democratic buy-in needed for 60 votes, chiefly over crypto ethics provisions.
frame_summary: The US crypto market-structure bill is grinding toward a late-July Senate push but still lacks the bipartisan buy-in it needs to pass.
cluster: Multilateral rulebooks splinter into national tracks
verbatim_quote: The U.S. Senate legislation that would regulate the crypto industry is wobbling forward in what are likely its final days as a viable effort for 2026, and advocates expect a new draft could emerge as soon as next week for potential Senate action later in the month.

title: Senate Banking Committee Advances Crypto Market Structure Bill
date_evidence: Senate Banking Committee Advances Crypto Market Structure Bill  05.21.26  url: /blogs/financial-services-law-advisor/2026/05/senate-banking-crypto-market-structure-bill
key_claim: On 14 May 2026 the Senate Banking Committee advanced its substitute Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, which now must be reconciled with the Senate Agriculture bill and the House CLARITY Act, with ethics language stripped to secure bipartisan committee support.
frame_summary: The Senate Banking Committee advanced its own crypto market-structure text, moving the US toward a bespoke federal digital-asset regime.
cluster: Multilateral rulebooks splinter into national tracks
verbatim_quote: On May 14, 2026, the Senate Banking Committee advanced the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act.

title: OECD releases Side-by-Side Package on Pillar Two Global Minimum Tax: Detailed review
date_evidence: 16 January 2026  OECD releases Side-by-Side Package on Pillar Two Global Minimum Tax: Detailed review
key_claim: On 5 January 2026 the OECD Inclusive Framework agreed a side-by-side package of Administrative Guidance with four new safe harbours that lets US-headquartered multinationals apply a Side-by-Side Safe Harbour, effectively carving them out of the global minimum tax.
frame_summary: The OECD's side-by-side package carves US-headquartered groups out of the global minimum tax, fracturing the multilateral Pillar Two consensus.
signals_supported: OECD Pillar Two US side-by-side carve-out
cluster: Multilateral rulebooks splinter into national tracks
verbatim_quote: On 5 January 2026, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development released a comprehensive package for a "side-by-side arrangement" with respect to the Pillar Two global minimum tax rules.
verbatim_list: In particular, United States-headquartered Multinational Enterprise Groups eligible to apply the Side-by-Side Safe Harbour should monitor the implementation in jurisdictions that potentially have taxing rights under the Income Inclusion Rule and Undertaxed Profits Rule.

title: Where State AI Legislation Stands Half Way Into 2026
date_evidence: <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-07-06T13:03:30.705Z">  Scott Babwah Brennen / Jul 6, 2026
key_claim: By 1 July 2026, 29 states had enacted 109 AI and 28 data-center laws, showing state AI lawmaking continuing at pace despite the Trump administration's December 2025 executive order and litigation task force aimed at preempting state AI rules.
frame_summary: US states keep enacting AI laws at pace despite a federal executive-order campaign to preempt them, deepening a domestic patchwork.
cluster: Multilateral rulebooks splinter into national tracks
verbatim_quote: By our count, as of July 1, states have enacted 109 AI and 28 data center laws.
verbatim_list: In December, 2025, President Trump issued an executive order creating a new AI Litigation Task Force charged with challenging state AI laws that were not “minimally burdensome.”

title: Where does the world stand on ISSB adoption?
date_evidence: May 2026 - Where does the world stand on ISSB adoption? | S&P Global. As of April 22, 2026, 28 jurisdictions have adopted the ISSB standards on a voluntary or mandatory basis.
key_claim: As of 22 April 2026, 28 jurisdictions had adopted the ISSB's IFRS S1/S2 sustainability-disclosure standards on a voluntary or mandatory basis, with a further 12 planning to, and interest rising as the EU pares back its own rules.
frame_summary: The ISSB's sustainability-disclosure standards keep gaining jurisdictions, consolidating into the global reporting baseline as the EU retreats.
cluster: Voluntary standards become the working baseline
